lines.trans: You know I have my own circumstances—my situation is not one where I can bring someone home.
At my house, my parents are there along with my older brother who is separated, plus my middle-school sister…
Everything else is fine, except your middle-school sister makes it impossible—she would spread rumors right away.
Yes, she is more than capable of doing that.
Cindy, we will lend you the money somehow, so how about staying at a five-star hotel?
If you go somewhere with a sweeping view of the Han River, rest a few days, and collect yourself…
CEO Byun knows me far too well—she will already be searching those hotels first.
Let me impose on you for just three days—in the ten years since starting as a trainee, I have never rested a single day.
It is only because I want to rest for three short days.
Why are you looking at me like that?

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like

meanings.note: Points to a place near the listener, and in casual or brisk speech is used to call out to someone whose name you do not know. RR: geogi.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright

examples.trans: I'm really fine.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

examples.trans: Who said that?

examples.trans: Is that really so?

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to emphasize immediate action or result.
E.g., 바로 옆 ('right next to'), 바로 그 사람 ('that very person').

meanings.note: Often carries surprise

examples.text: 어렵게 생각하면 한없이 어렵지만 쉽게 생각하면 별거 아니에요.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
